clue.text: Bear right entering a foreign country, officer

indicators.note: entering means the letter for right goes inside the country's letters

parts.note: the USA, a foreign country from a British paper's point of view
a major is an army officer

explanation.surface: A bear wanders across a border, and an officer is on hand to deal with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts R inside USA to make URSA; the Great Bear is the constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear constellation goes by its Latin name, so the word is a straight synonym.

clue.text: City in which you can find Girl Guide

indicators.note: in which you can find says the girl's letters sit inside the city's

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
she stands for a girl or woman

explanation.surface: A town where you might come across a Girl Guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl Guide' reads as one phrase, but it splits: the girl goes inside the city, and 'Guide' on its own is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats, so he guides them.

clue.text: Can go under water, and is explicable

explanation.surface: Something that dissolves in water also has an explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: A soluble substance dissolves in liquid, and a soluble problem can be solved.

clue.text: Contraband — that's nonsense!

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses talk of smuggled goods as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicitly distilled liquor is called by this name, and so is foolish talk.

clue.text: Seriously, a pink jar got broken

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone solemnly reports that a pink jar has been smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means setting jest aside and speaking in earnest.

clue.text: Epitaph for a disreputable person

explanation.surface: A tombstone inscription for a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials for 'rest in peace' appear on gravestones, and a rip is also an old word for a rake or rogue.

clue.text: Confusion apparent in such a vocabulary

indicators.note: apparent in says the answer can be seen sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone's choice of words is causing chaos and muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparent in' points at the letters running across 'such a vocabulary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread disorder, a synonym for chaos and confusion.

clue.text: Has to accept King Henry's unfeeling

indicators.note: to accept means the word has takes in the letter for king

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted royal is forced to agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts R inside HAS to make HARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh treatment is cruel and lacks sympathy.

clue.text: First class orders given involving soldiers…

indicators.note: involving means the shuffled letters wrap round the soldiers
orders as a verb means arranges, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Top-grade instructions are issued to the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' rearranges the clue word to give VINGE, and 'involving' wraps those letters round the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintage means of the highest quality, like a fine wine of a good year.

clue.text: …to provide the finishing touch, army gives finale in first class style

parts.note: 'to cap it all' means to crown or complete things

indicators.note: finale means the closing letter of the word army

explanation.surface: The army puts on a superb grand finale to round off the show.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read as 'cap it all', then Y, the last letter of 'army', follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitally means excellently, in a splendid way.

clue.text: Wine I will put into a barrow

indicators.note: put into says the contraction goes inside the wine's letters

parts.note: hock is a German white wine
I'll is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: A bottle of wine is to be loaded into a wheelbarrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrow' is not the garden cart. It is an ancient burial mound.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is an earth mound, so it is a small hill.

clue.text: Vegetarian food and drink after good scores

indicators.note: after says the drink comes later in the answer than the scores

parts.note: a par is a good score on a golf hole
a nip is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: A golfer celebrates good rounds with a meatless meal and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR is the standard score for a golf hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a root vegetable, so it is meat-free food.

clue.text: Invests in eggs — about a billion .

indicators.note: about means the eggs wrap round the letter for a billion

parts.note: roes are fish eggs
B is an abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: A financier puts money into eggs, around a billion pounds' worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invests' here means dresses in ceremonial garments, not puts money in.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is to clothe them formally, as one does with ceremonial garb.

clue.text: Heart's not broken — that's the point

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lover says their heart is not broken, and that is the whole point.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the compass points, the direction halfway between two cardinal ones.

clue.text: Heraldic officer with coloured garment on

parts.note: rouged means coloured with red make-up
a rag is a scrappy item of clothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: An official of arms wears a dyed costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Rouge Dragon is one of the pursuivants of the College of Arms in London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a junior officer at the English College of Arms.

clue.text: Bond starts to tackle international espionage

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: James Bond sets out to deal with international spying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' invites 007, which fits the espionage, but it is the definition: a link or tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a connection or link binding two things, which is a bond.

clue.text: Perched up on Church House, above a stretch of water

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: sat means perched
a manse is a minister's house

explanation.surface: A bird sits atop a church building, overlooking the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SAT into TAS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea lies between Australia and New Zealand, a large expanse of ocean.

clue.text: Brazil discovered thus briefly

explanation.surface: An explorer's terse report on finding a South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brazil is also a nut, and a nut is found in its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means put concisely; it also says where a Brazil nut is found.

clue.text: Deliver in prepaid container of lead

indicators.note: in means the delivery word is placed inside the envelope's letters

parts.note: an SAE is a stamped addressed envelope
to turn in is to hand over or deliver

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a postage-paid box made of heavy metal.
explanation.walkthrough: SAE is a British abbreviation for stamped addressed envelope. Saturn was the alchemists' planet for lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine can mean relating to lead, since alchemy linked the metal with Saturn.

clue.text: One not usually centre stage

indicators.note: not usually says the letters are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone who normally avoids the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a spy keeps out of the spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy works covertly, keeping out of public view rather than taking the spotlight.

clue.text: Dog on river boat

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed

explanation.surface: A dog stands on a riverboat.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a ship built for carrying coal.

clue.text: On the ball, pass quickly

explanation.surface: A footballer is alert and moves the ball on fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is slang for sharp or alert, and time is said to fly when it goes by quickly.

clue.text: Bit of music provided by pop stars for their admirers?

definitions.text: provided by pop stars for their admirers?

explanation.surface: Musicians perform a short piece for their devoted followers.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, it is the food a fan is served, playfully suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a short trumpet flourish; split, it is what pop idols serve their followers.

clue.text: Turn round to measure a reptile

indicators.note: round says the run of pieces is turned back to front as a whole

parts.note: a rota is a list of people's turns
a gill is a measure of liquid, a quarter of a pint

explanation.surface: Someone spins about to size up a crocodile-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reverses all three pieces together as one run, so the answer is the whole charade read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is a large crocodilian, one kind of reptile.

clue.text: :The place for putting information about engineers

indicators.note: about means the information letters go round the engineers

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A noticeboard where details of engineers are posted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is golf, not placing: putts are played on a green.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course, putts are played on the smooth turf around the hole.

clue.text: Update about 12 women's…

parts.note: re means about or concerning
12 across is the compass point, abbreviated NE
W is an abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A news update on twelve women continues into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' refers to the answer of 12 across, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to refresh or bring it up to date.

clue.text: Unlawfully take forty winks, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: forty winks is a short nap, a rest

explanation.surface: Someone steals a little sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to seize forcibly, taking something away by violence.

clue.text: … pay — it's put back to await settlement

indicators.note: put back means the letters are written in reverse order

parts.note: its, taken as written
to pend is to remain undecided, awaiting settlement

explanation.surface: Women's wages are held over until a dispute is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns ITS into STI.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular salary, especially a clergyman's.

clue.text: It holds water and raises bananas

indicators.note: raises in a down clue means the word is read upward, from the bottom

parts.note: bananas is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Something that keeps water in also grows a fruit crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' means crazy, not the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is a barrier built to hold back a body of water.

clue.text: Expression — forbidding one

parts.note: grim means stern or forbidding
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone wears a stern, off-putting look.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of disgust or pain.

clue.text: Garment worn after 30 days

indicators.note: after says the worn piece goes later in the answer

parts.note: April has 30 days, abbreviated Apr
something worn is on, as in having a coat on

explanation.surface: An item of clothing is put on after a month.
explanation.walkthrough: '30 days' stands for one month with that many days, April.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a protective garment tied over the front of one's clothes.

clue.text: Cinema met with difficulties showing what went into Sweeney Todd's pies

definitions.text: what went into Sweeney Todd's pies

indicators.note: with difficulties signals the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A cinema showing a film about the demon barber hits problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the fictional London barber whose victims were baked into pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopped flesh is the filling in the legend; minced meat in pies, and the phrase for being destroyed.
